# The Things Below · Book II, pp. 412–437
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	412
P	They are older than the world. They are <b>primordial entities</b> (page 298) of darkness, chaos, and corruption.
P	When light first filled the void, they were huddled in the shadows. When matter coalesced, they were there, chewing at its edges. When the First Creators thought "I am me" and named themselves, Those Who Dwelt in Darkness sought their ruin. They whispered lies and stoked egos. They urged the Creators to war amongst themselves. To lay waste to their creations. To let chaos reign.
P	But the First Creators saw the lies for what they were. They saw the danger posed by the Eldest of Evils. But they saw, too, the utility of such deception.
P	And so, the Creators laid a trap. They came together to forge the world itself: matter and energy, land and sea and sky, life and death.
P	They set in motion a system so vast and intricate and wondrous that They Who Whispered could not help but be jealous, could not help but try to destroy it.
P	When the Terrible Ones moved to destroy the world, the First Creators sprung their trap.
P	They folded the world around the Things That Knew Only Hate, sealed them away in rock and stone, bound them in the earth itself. The world— this world, what would become our world—became their tether and their prison.
P	And they, so shackled, became the Things Below.
PAGE	413
H2	The Time of Cataclysm
HR
P	No prison is perfect. With the slow turn of ages, the bindings weakened. The Things Below whispered once again, and those whispers found ears.
P	The <b>Stone Lords</b> (page 382) learned firsthand the chaos that those whispers could unleash. They found the cracks in the world-prison and laid great seals upon them. For a time, the whispers were quiet.
P	But the <b>Green Lords</b> (page 210) remembered those whispers and what they promised, and called upon the Things Below to crush the traitorous <b>Fae</b> (page 94). The Green Lords were ultimately defeated, but the real damage had been done: the bindings were weakened. The whispers of the Things Below had returned, had become a song.
P	The Stone Lords' own servants heard that song. Sorcerers arose among them, gathered followings, then cults. In secret, they laid their plans and spread their lies. When the time was right, the sorcerers broke the seals and ushered in the Time of Cataclysm.
P	The Stone Lords' cities sank. Mobs of their servants turned against them. In the north, a dark and terrible howling arose and the <b>Rime</b> <b>Lords</b> (page 316) sacrificed themselves to stop it. A wave of horrors burrowed up from the <b>Flats</b> (page 126), bringing the last of the <b>Tempest</b> <b>Lords</b> low (page 398). The Things Below stoked the jealousies and fears of the <b>Forge Lords</b> (page 156), turning them against each other.
P	The time of the Makers was over.
PAGE	414
H2	The current age
HR
P	In the aftermath of the Makers' fall, the would-be sorcerer-kings of the <b>Barrow</b> <b>Builders</b> (page 34) came to dominate the World's End. For generations, the region—and perhaps the wider world—knew only horror, and suffering, and war.
P	And yet: the power of the Things Below waned. For centuries now, they have lain mostly quiet in the earth. What brought those dark times to an end? That's for you and your table to decide, but perhaps…
E	the <b>gods</b> themselves (page 178) intervened;
E	mortal heroes worked a great binding, empowered by great sacrifice;
E	the brave and the desperate rose up across the land, toppling sorcerers and banishing horrors one-by-one;
E	the world began to heal itself and renew its bindings;
E	the Things Below—sated on destruction and woe—simply tired and withdrew;
E	some combination of the above; or
E	something else entirely.
P	Whatever caused the Things Below to fall back, their retreat was incomplete. Some places remain touched by their influence, some creatures stained to the heart.
P	Objects of power linger, corrupting the unwitting, and some of these—like the sorcerers of old—dance in the dark to a nightmarish tune.
P	Of late, within the past generation or so, tremors have coursed through different quarters of the World's End. Do prisoners in the depths strain once more against their shackles?
H2	Hooks
B	A local unwittingly offers sacrifice to a corrupted spirit, gaining power; the spirit asks for (and offers) more
B	A conundrum vexes the PCs; consulting <b>a black menhir</b> (page 425) might help
B	<b>Crinwin</b> (page 58) have started to worship at a <b>corrupted site</b> (page 422) becoming corrupted in turn
B	<b>An antiquarian</b> (page 260) is secretly a thrall to a Thing Below, and seeks to unleash a more powerful servant
B	A spot in the fields around Stonetop goes bad, festering like an infected boil, corrupted by a discarded artifact

H2	Lore
HR
P	<b>Everyone knows:</b>
B	Evil things are bound deep within the earth
B	Sometimes, they send forth demons to wreak havoc upon the world
B	Deep water is the most likely place for such horrors to emerge
B	<b>Marshedge</b> (page 274) keeps such horrors at bay by constantly burning bendis root
P	<b>One might know:</b>
B	About the Time of Cataclysm and what came after
B	The name, titles, aspects, powers, or minions of a given Thing Below
B	How their power corrupts places, artifacts, people, beasts, and spirits
B	How to bind, cleanse, or ward off their taint/power/minions
B	That unclean things recoil from bendis root smoke, but truly fierce or willful ones can overcome it
B	That bronze is bane to the Things Below, and that <b>orichalcum</b> (page 162) is even more effective
B	The difference between corrupted beings and emanations
P	<b>Very few know:</b>
B	Of their true nature
B	How they came to be imprisoned
B	Any way to truly destroy one
H2	Questions
Q	What frightening tale from childhood featured the Things Below?
Q	What little thing do villagers do to ward off their attention or influence?
Q	When did you first feel their presence? What happened? What still haunts you about that experience to this day?
Q	What place nearby is said to be tainted by their influence? What sign marks it as such?
Q	How do the locals speak of them? In hushed tones? In dire sermons? Somewhere in between?
Q	When was the last time the village dealt with a demon, cult, or sorcerer?
H2	Demons
P	In truth, there's no such thing as demons. Or rather, "demon" is not a meaningful term. It's often used to refer to <b>emanations</b> (page 436) of or <b>beings corrupted</b> (page 432) by the Things Below. But folks might use the term to apply to any number of supernatural terrors. If it's hostile, magical, and has (or can take) a physical form, someone is likely to call it a demon.
PAGE	416
H2	Themes
HR
P	When you introduce a Thing—or more likely, when you introduce a site, artifact, or danger associated with one—choose or roll 2 or more prompts from the theme table here. Combine the results and see where they take you. Alternatively, pick one of the <b>established Things Below</b> (page 419), and use its themes.
P	1d12 theme
HR
P	1 Darkness/cold/despair: the swallowing of light, warmth, and hope (obsidian, hoarfrost)
P	2 Denial/shame/secrets/deceit: the rejection of truth, forgiveness, trust (pearls, eyes, masks)
P	3 Delusion/delirium/nightmare: the loss of self, the breaking of minds and wills (quicksilver, mirrors, reflections)
P	4 Hunger/need/addiction: lack and desperation, the howling want (wind, fangs, meat)
P	5 Cruelty/torture/violence/rage: the urge to hurt, kill, and dominate (red crystal, spilled blood)
P	6 Destruction/chaos/ruin/ignorance:
P	the tower crumbling; anxiety and loss (fire, ash, dust)
P	7 Wounds/injury/pain: the rending of flesh, the breaking of bone (blood, bones, claws, blades)
P	8 Corruption/disease/decay: the loss of strength, wholeness, wellness (vermin, poison, acid, filth)
P	9 Gluttony/greed/jealousy: the need for more, ever more (mouths, serpents, gems, swarms)
P	10 Confinement/suffocation/pressure/ abuse: the crushing weight of helplessness (chains, water, earth)
P	11 Mutation/transformation/roiling flesh: the malleability of the body (wax, clay, slime, tentacles)
P	12 Death/undeath/loss/grief: the end of all things, the refusal to let go (skulls, tombs, pyres)

H2	Creating a Thing
HR
P	As it becomes necessary to flesh out a Thing Below, combine its themes (previous page) with 2 or more aspects to inspire your descriptions of it. Choose or roll an instinct, or invent one of your own.
P	If a Thing Below becomes an ongoing source of problems for the PCs (and it probably will), then give it a name and one or more grandiose titles. Write it up as a threat (a <i>magical entity</i>).
P	1d12 aspect
HR
P	1 Chitin/shell/carapace/armor
P	2 An elder/a crone/a stooped old man
P	3 Fire/light/haze/cloud/vortex/void
P	4 Horns/wings/tail(s)/hooves
P	5 The inanimate, animated/an amalgamation of things
P	6 Many-limbed/many-headed/ many-eyed/many-bodied
P	7 Moisture/tentacles/slime/ooze
P	8 A predator/a warrior/a warlord/ a ruler
P	9 Scales/sinew/suppleness
P	10 Skulls/bones/corpses/death
P	11 Vastness/immensity
P	12 A youth/a child/an infant Remember that the Things Below are not bound by constraints of biology, physics, or reality. Make their aspects impossible and weird, things of fever-dream and drugfueled vision.
P	1d12 instinct
HR
P	1 To stoke conflict, confusion, distrust
P	2 To erode hope/faith/honor/ self-image
P	3 To hide/bury/smother things or ideas
P	4 To deprive others of what they need
P	5 To inflict harm, cruelly and unnecessarily
P	6 To desecrate/mutilate/ruin things of value
P	7 To shock/terrify/horrify others
P	8 To wantonly devour and consume
P	9 To befoul and corrupt beauty/ strength/dignity
P	10 To fight and hurt and kill and rage and hurt some more
P	11 To dominate, punish, and crush
P	12 To simply destroy, nothing more and nothing less Tweak the instinct you choose to reflect your growing understanding of this particular Thing Below.

H2	Names & titles
HR
P	The true names of the Things Below are nigh impossible for humans to comprehend, much less pronounce. What names we have for them are crude approximations. Still, they work well enough to call upon their power.
P	To name a Thing Below, try one of these:
B	Pick an unpleasant word or concept, translate it into a language you and your players don't know ("hunger" >> "Hlad" in Czech)
B	Take the name of a supernatural entity from pop culture, literature, or another game; change it a little or a lot ("Dagon" >> "Daagon").
B	Combine short, unlikely sounds, often with apostrophes to denote short pauses or inflection ("Hec'tumel")
B	Some combination of the above
P	Then, give each Thing one or more evocative titles, keeping in mind the themes and aspects already established. Look to the lists below for inspiration, altering word forms to suit (i.e., "suppurate" might becomes Suppurating, Suppuration, or Suppurator).
P	<b>Article/preoposition:</b> the, a, an, who, which, that, of, in, on, through, with, without, o <b>Verb:</b> bargain, bleed, break, bring, burn, burrow, bury, butcher, chew, consume, crawl, crush, dance, deceive, deny, desire, despoil, destroy, eat, end, engulf, feed, fester, flense, freeze, haunt, hide, hoard, howl, hunger, keep, know, lack, laugh, lie, melt, offer, promise, rage, rend, roil, rot, scatter, scurry, seep, shape, shatter, sing, slaughter, sleep, slough, smother, snuff, spoil, starve, steal, strain, suppurate, swallow, swarm, topple, unravel, wallow, want, weave, whisper, wither, etc.
P	<b>Adjective:</b> all-consuming, awful, black, blackest, broken, crimson, cruel, dark, dead, desperate, eldest, false, forty, endless, first, forgotten, forlorn, gray, great, hidden, hundred, hungry, implacable, inexorable, lost, mad, many, pale, pallid, red, rusty, secret, terrible, thousand, unkind, unliving, vast, wrathful, yellow <b>Role:</b> child, daughter, father, heir, herald, king, lady, last, lord, master, mistress, mother, prince, princess, thief, queen, son, tyrant, etc.
H3	Example names
P	Use these as a starting point to develop your own Things.
B	Ha'z-Ra'iel, Herald of Grief, Thief of a Thousand Hopes
B	Na'ieraak, the Liar in Shadows, He Who Freezes the Heart
B	Unhlef 'k, the Nightmare that Eats, the Dream with Teeth
B	Ta'l Themyin, Burning Child, Cruel Infant, Prince of Rage
B	H'nisat, the Suppuration, the Wound that Festers
B	Hakog, False Wind and Last Whisper of Deceit
B	Lalacheewa, Who Sups on Ash and Sorrow

H2	For We Are Many
HR
P	The Things Below are legion, varying wildly in power and predilection, activity and ambition. Some are whispered of by peoples far and wide. Others are local terrors, gnawing at a single thread of the world that binds them.
P	Following are half a dozen Things Below that may or may not exist in your game.

H3	Daagon, Who Waits in Deep Waters
P	Threat (<i>magical entity</i>)
P	<b>Themes</b> gluttony/greed/jealousy, roiling flesh/mutation/transformation <b>Instinct</b> to take from the surface, to never let go
P	• Send forth minions to do its bidding
P	• Offer power, wealth, immortality
P	• Demand a sacrifice
P	• Twist its servants into wet and wriggling things
P	Those foolish enough to brave deep water will tell you: something lurks below. Something patient, something vast, an abyssal mouth opening into a belly that can never be filled. Its countless squirming servants brave the dry and choking land to gather flesh, to gather bone. To steal all wealth and beauty. To take lives full of hope and promise, and feed them to the yawning dark wet jaws.
P	See also: <b>Blackwater Lake</b> (page 48), the secrets of <b>Gordin's Delve</b> (page 190), and the <b>Ring of Daagon</b> (page 560).
HR
ICON	icons/sea.svg
H3	El'rash-Orra, Lord of Orbs, the Many-Eyes
P	Threat (<i>magical entity</i>)
P	<b>Themes</b> denial/shame/secrets/deceit, delusion/delirium/nightmare <b>Instinct</b> to reveal all manner of ugliness
P	• Spy on someone's actions, desires, shames
P	• Give knowledge (wanted or not) via dreams/visions
P	• Twist someone's senses (of reality, of themselves)
P	Should you find yourself alone, and yet convinced that you're being watched, it's best not to turn and look. For if you do, you might see a great and disembodied eye. Or worse: a faceless sovereign upon a silver throne, brandishing a silver orb. And should it stand, and let its robes fall open, it will be as the night sky with countless twinkling eyes that see all shames and doubts, all regrets, all guilts and secret fears that have ever been or those that might yet be. Lo! It will show them all to you! Gladly, it will show you! Whether you wish to see or not.
P	See also: the <b>Staff of the Lidless Orb</b> (page 540).

H3	Hec'tumel, Pale Serpent! Slitherer In Darkness! Death Is Its Eyes!
P	Threat (<i>magical entity</i>)
P	<b>Themes</b> darkness/cold/despair, undeath/ death/loss/grief <b>Instinct</b> to smother life, hope, and light
P	• Sense powerful longings/emotions
P	• Offer services, secrets, or power
P	• Twist a bargain to its favor 'Tis a pale thing, a dead thing, a long reptilian creature with skulls where it should have eyes. It slithers through darksome, bone-strewn caves. Caves that drip with tears and lost hopes. It raised up the first sorcerers, gave them the power they craved. It asked only for little things, harmless things, things they'd never miss. And it delighted, yesss it delighted so, when the gifts it gave brought their recipients low. Brought them low, and everything around them, yesss.

H3	Hlad, the Devourer, the Eternal Maw
P	Threat (<i>magical entity</i>)
P	<b>Themes</b> hunger/need/addiction, destruction/chaos/ruin/ignorance
P	<b>Instinct</b> to consume reality
P	• Erode strength, wholeness, life
P	• Draw in the weak-willed
P	• Grow in strength and power
P	The Eternal Maw is a hole in reality, a howling vortex of destruction. To hear its song is to know that all things will end, to wish for the respite of oblivion. To look upon it is to see the void, to know the futility of struggle. To touch it is to feel all strength and courage fail, to face a terrible choice. Will you submit to its implacable hunger? Or will you become one of its infinite mouths?
P	See also: the <b>Hungering Maw of Hlad</b> (page 572).

H3	Y'aaw'kara, the Howling Wind, the Flayer of Flesh
P	Threat (<i>magical entity</i>)
P	<b>Themes</b> hunger/need/addiction, cruelty/ torture/violence/rage, wounds/ injury/pain <b>Instinct</b> to spread pain and misery
P	• Sense or amplify hunger/fear/ anger/pain
P	• Offer the strength of cruelty
P	• Inflict the <b>Howling Curse</b> (page 492) on someone
P	To the people of the far north, Y'aaw'kara's voice is constant as the wind. For he is the angry word. He is the gnawing winter hunger. He is the dream of vengeance upon those who have wronged you, or those who simply have more. Greet him, and you shall see a starving wolf with the body of a starving man, bleeding from a dozen wounds. Listen to him, and you shall hear his wheezing breath, howling like a blizzard gale. Invite him in, and never be prey again.
P	See also: <b>Barrier Pass</b> (page 26), the <b>Whitefang Mountains</b> (page 480).

H2	Corrupted sites
HR
P	These are places where the influence of the Things Below has taken hold, where their power seeps into the world. If the site itself hasn't been established, combine the terrain in which it is located with a feature.
P	1d12 feature
HR
P	1 Nothing to mark it but the terrain itself
P	2-3 A distinctive (un)natural landmark (big tree, natural arch, spring, etc.)
P	4 Signs of great destruction (ash fields, crevasse, lava flow, mudslide, etc.)
P	5 A beast's lair/burrow/den
P	6 A tomb/barrow/memorial, left by the locals or their ancestors
P	7 An old dwelling/gathering place of the locals or their ancestors
P	8 A ruin of <b>the Makers</b> (page 264), or a lingering sign of their presence
P	9-12 Deep water, the depths obscure, conceals the site (roll 1d8)
P	Once the site is established, pick or roll its themes (page 416) to identify the nature of the Thing corrupting the place (or, if you know the Thing is one already established, apply its themes to the site).
P	Pick or roll the cause and severity of the corruption. Populate the place with <b>artifacts</b> (page 424) and <b>dangers</b> (page 428) associated with the Things Below, plus discoveries and dangers appropriate to the surrounding area.
P	1d12 cause
HR
P	1 Erosion/shifting earth/ the implacable passage of time
P	2 A failed attempt to wield primordial power
P	3-5 An artifact/a sorcerer's bones/ remains of a corrupted beast/etc., left to fester*
P	6-8 An offering of flesh/blood/trauma, intentional or not*
P	9-10 A summoning/an invocation/ a misguided invitation*
P	11-12 A seal or binding that kept prior corruption in check, now weakened* (roll d10 again for the original corruption)
P	* Decide whether this was intentional, or have someone roll the Die of Fate (1-2:
P	intentional; 3-4 misguided; 5-6 accidental/ incidental). If it was intentional or misguided, who did it and why? If accidental, what happened?
P	1d12 severity
HR
P	1-3 A shunned place: full of <b>disquiet</b> <b>and unease</b> (page 428), not actively dangerous but where it's easy to draw upon their power
P	4-6 A hungry place: full of <b>whispers</b> <b>and visions</b> (page 428), calling the unwholesome, trapping and consuming the unwary
P	7-9 A poisonous place: full of <b>unnatural</b> <b>phenomena</b> (page 429), corrupting those who visit
P	10-11 A spawning place: where <b>emanations</b> (page 436) congeal and manifest
P	12 A wound in the world: spreading rot, bleeding horror, getting worse The dangers from a lower level of severity can be found in higher levels, too. A hungry place is full of whispers and visions but perhaps disquiet and unease as well.
PAGE	423
P	If a corrupted site will be a source of ongoing trouble, write it up as a <b>threat</b> (a <i>MacGuffin</i>), with an impending doom and grim portents that reflect it getting worse. Look to the list of causes (previous page) for ideas about what could make a corrupted site worse, and what sort of new dangers it might start to manifest.
H3	Cleansing corrupted sites
P	The Things Below are loathe to relinquish what power they have in the world, but they can be bested with bravery, cunning, and knowledge. Some PCs (like the Blessed) will have powers or arcana that let them bind or contain the evil in a place. Absent such power, the PCs will need to Make a Plan. Consider such requirements as:
C	You must learn the name of the Thing Below that taints this place
C	You must find the seed of corruption within the site
C	You must create/obtain __, with which to bind the evil (next column)
C	You must repair the bindings that previously held back the corruption
C	You'll need the help of a powerful spirit/Fae
C	It'll take days/weeks of prayer and ritual cleansing
C	You must wait until high noon/the solstice/the equinox/the full moon
C	The best you can do is stop it from getting worse
C	It will require burning sacks of bendis root (Value 2)
C	You'll risk being corrupted yourselves
C	You'll risk making things much worse To bind corruption, one might use…
E	a tree, especially an elder tree;
E	a large piece of stone/crystal/amber/ <b>dark ice</b> (page 322);
E	a ring of runes, deeply etched;
E	a spike/vessel of bronze, <b>orichalcum</b> (page 162), or <b>black iron</b> (page 307)
E	a <b>Fae domain</b> (page 102);
E	a barrow/cairn/vault/urn/vessel, sealed and sanctified;
E	a perpetual holy flame;
E	the bones of a pure soul, properly carved and prepared;
E	some combination of the above; or
E	something else entirely.
HR
P	<i>The PCs are following the river Sruth</i> <i>to its source. I've decided that they'll pass</i> <i>a corrupted site along the river. I've no</i> <i>particulars in mind, so I roll a 6 for feature (tomb/barrow/memorial of the locals</i> <i>or their ancestors). That makes me think</i> <i>of the</i> <b><i>Barrow Builders</i></b> (page 34)<i>.</i>
P	<i>For themes, I roll 6 (destruction/chaos/</i> <i>ruin/ignorance with "fire, ash") and 8</i> <i>(corruption/disease/decay with "vermin,</i> <i>poison, acid, filth"). I roll a 2 for the cause</i> <i>(attempt to wield primordial power), and</i> <i>a 3 for severity (a shunned place).</i>
P	<i>I discard my first instinct to make it a</i> <i>sorcerer's tomb and decide instead that</i> <i>it's a cairn on a low hill, overlooking</i> <i>the river. Inside lie the remains of a</i> <i>sorcerer-king's child. The sorcerer tried</i> <i>to call them back from beyond the Last</i> <i>Door, but succeeded only in blighting</i> <i>the hillside with fell power. To this day,</i> <i>the stones are hot to the touch, steaming in rain and snow. Nothing grows</i> <i>there, and a swath of sickly, barren soil</i> <i>runs down the hill to the river, where it</i> <i>becomes bubbling, poisonous muck.</i>

H2	Red crystal
HR
P	Pulsing, warm, and thirsting for blood, like cruelty solidified. Red crystal is associated with the most violent and hateful of the Things Below. It grows in places they have corrupted, sometimes jutting from the earth in prodigious quantities. Creatures corrupted by the Things Below might have claws or fangs or antlers made of the stuff.
P	Red crystal has subtle effects, but can be put to many uses. For example:
B	Those with power over others find it fascinating; the victimized find it terrifying (plenty of people find it both)
B	It causes tempers to flare, stokes resentment, pushes folks to act on impulse
B	It absorbs any blood it touches, growing warmer and glowing brighter
B	Sorcerers can fashion it into potent talismans, or use it to fuel their magic
B	Demon-hunters sometimes use it to lure their prey into traps
H2	Artifacts
HR
H3	Various treasures
B	A <b>crude stone figurine</b> of some beast, the claws and fangs exaggerated and seemingly stained with blood (Value 0)
B	A <b>pot full of dust</b>◇ (3 uses, <i>fragile</i>, Value 1 to the right person) that causes a racking cough, weakness, maybe even paralysis
B	A <b>lantern</b>◇ (5 hours, <i>reach</i>, <i>area</i>, <i>magical</i>, Value 1) made of twisted black metal; its flame casts pale light that leaches color and chills the air
B	A <b>chunk of red crystal</b> (previous column), shaped to look like a leering skull (Value 1 to the right person)
B	A ◇◇ <b>large tome of supple vellum</b> (best not to ask the source) full of ramblings in an archaic dialect, unsettling images, and arcane diagrams (Value 2)
B	A <b>human(ish) skull</b>◇ but with six eye sockets and jutting lower tusks, carved with disturbing patterns and inlaid with silver (Value 3 to the right buyer)
B	A <b>twisted elder tree</b>, found with deer licking at its sap and ignoring the approach of threats; the sap can be refined into a highly addictive drug

H3	A black menhir
P	<i>magical</i>, <i>immobile</i>
P	A number of these megaliths have appeared in the <b>Great Wood</b> (page 200) of late. They are jagged chunks of basalt, tall as a tall lad, etched with intricate patterns that could be writing, almost. The earth around them is broken and disturbed. They are unmarred by moss or lichen, untouched by shoot or vine.
P	When you <b><i>study the intricate markings and</i></b> <b><i>let your mind wander</i></b>, you receive a vision or intuition about the current situation.
P	The GM will describe it. But first, roll
P	+WIS: <b>on a 10+</b>, pick only 1; <b>on a 7-9</b>, pick
P	2; <b>on a 6-</b>, alas, all 3 are true.
B	Part of what you learn is false or misleading (but what?)
B	You start to suffer nightmares, of horrors shifting in the earth
B	The menhir asks a question about your shame, guilt, or fears—answer truly

H3	A deep, dark shaft
P	A hole in the ground, maybe 5 feet wide, at least 100 feet deep, ending in a watery chamber or underground lake that contains a <b>Mouth of Daagon</b> (page 55).
P	When you <b><i>linger near the shaft</i></b>, answer one of the following:
Q	Of whom are you most jealous, and why?
Q	What do you wish to possess, more than anything?
Q	When did you last feel trapped and helpless?
P	When you <b><i>toss something down the shaft</i></b>, Daagon devours it utterly. When <b><i>someone</i></b> <b><i>falls down the shaft</i></b>, they are gone, body and soul.
P	When you <b><i>feed the Mouth of Daagon someone or something beloved</i></b> (by anyone, not just you), Daagon gives you a gift.
P	1d6 gift
HR
P	1 A physical change (scales, rubbery flesh, gills, a tentacle, etc.)

P	4 A "priceless" item (Value 4)
P	5 A way to best your rivals or defeat your enemies

ICON	icons/treasure.svg
H3	An iron spider
P	<i>magical</i>, <i>indestructible</i>
P	About the size of one's palm, half an inch thick, rusted around the edges, with legs folded up on the back. A hidden button makes the legs extend and reveals their bladed tips. Sometimes, when you go to retrieve it, it's not quite where you left it.
P	The spider is hungry when you find it.
P	When you <b><i>plunge the hungry spider into a</i></b> <b><i>person's flesh</i></b>, they lose 1d4 HP every few seconds until it's torn free (1d8 damage, <i>messy</i>, ignores armor). Should the spider drain them to 0 HP, it becomes sated.
P	When you <b><i>plunge the sated spider into a</i></b> <b><i>person's flesh</i></b>, they take 1 damage (ignores armor) and will not age for 1d10 years. If they are middle aged or older, they regain some vigor of their youth. Then, the spider becomes hungry.
P	Each time someone uses the spider to extend their life, their features change subtly, becoming blander, waxier, more pallid, less specific. Should they die after exceeding their mortal lifespan, they become a <b>revenant</b> (page 80), hungering for blood.
ICON	icons/treasure.svg
H3	An obsidian pendant
P	<i>magical</i>
P	A lump of volcanic glass, impossibly black, set in a pendant and hanging from a leather cord. The glass sucks up light from nearby sources, causing them to dim. (The sun and moon are unaffected, as they are far, far away.) More subtly, the pendant also sucks up kindness, making individuals in its presence more callous and self-centered.
P	When you <b><i>wear or carry the pendant</i></b> <b><i>openly for a few minutes or more</i></b>, your eyes adjust and can see clearly in all but pitch darkness. But also, your instinct for the session becomes "Callousness: to disregard the feelings, needs, or wellbeing of others."

H3	A serpentine armband

P	Cast from silver that never seems to tarnish, with what appear to be two small rubies in its eye sockets. It seems like it might not fit—but what do you know, it does.

Roll +CON: <b>on a</b> <b>10+</b>, you'll get over it; <b>on a 7-9</b>, either put the armband back on (and keep it there) or mark a debility; <b>on a 6-</b>, you cannot sleep until you put the armband on and wear it openly around others.

H2	Dangers

ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Disquiet and unease
P	Places touched by the Things Below are <i>wrong</i>. Most people and natural beasts shun such places, and spirits of the wild either flee or become tainted themselves.
P	As you describe the environment or make any of the GM moves below, show off the themes (page 416) and instinct (page 417) of the Thing Below behind all this.
P	• Introduce something ominous (a cold spot, a dramatic gust of wind, mist/fog, a foul stench, etc.)
P	• Make something seem worse than it is
P	• Imply that allies might betray them
P	• Ask about their fears/doubts/shames/ animosities
P	• Have an NPC get edgy/act weird/ freak out
P	• Reveal a lack of natural spirits, or only unsavory ones, plus a hateful power that yearns to be called forth
HR
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Whispers and visions
P	Where the influence of the Things Below is strong, people hear voices, see things that aren't there, experience powerful emotions.
P	As you describe the environment or make any of the GM moves below, show off the themes (page 416) and instinct (page 417) of the Thing Below behind all this.
P	• Twist their senses
P	• Lure them deeper/closer
P	• Keep them from sleeping
P	• Fill them with growing dread
P	• Overwhelm them with <b>terror</b> (next page)
P	• Stir an unsavory emotion (anger, jealousy, despair, hate, resentment, etc.)
P	• Whisper a suggestion or compulsion
P	• Show an NPC struggling to keep it together, to keep control
P	• Have an NPC succumb to the whispers/ their fear/their emotions
P	When you <b><i>do as the whispers suggest</i></b>, mark XP and they can now compel you.
P	When <b><i>the whispers compel you</i></b>, mark XP if you do as they bid. If you resist, roll +WIS:
P	<b>on a 10+</b>, do as you wish; <b>on a 7-9</b>, choose 1:
B	Act as compelled, but divert yourself at the last moment
B	Struggle for control until someone/ something snaps you out of it
B	Hurt yourself (1d4 damage, ignores armor) and immediately regain control
P	<b>On a 6-</b>, pick 1:
B	Mark a debility, lose 1d4 HP, and do something drastic to regain control
B	Run with it, coming to later having done gods-know-what
PAGE	429
HR
ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Terror
P	When you <b><i>are overwhelmed with</i></b> <b><i>terror</i></b>, and do anything other than flee, hide, or cower, pick 1:
B	Work yourself up to the task (ask the GM what happens in the meantime)
B	Act rashly and recklessly (incurring additional cost or consequence)
B	Mark a debility of the GM's choice, and act immediately

H3	Unnatural phenomena
P	As the corruption of a site grows stronger, the world starts to twist and unravel. As you describe the environment or make any of the GM moves below, show off the themes (page 416) and instinct (page 417) of the Thing Below behind all this.
P	• Present something impossible and disturbing (bleeding walls, water pooling on the ceiling, darkness that light won't penetrate, etc.)
P	• Have light sources dim/sputter/snuff out
P	• Reveal that food has spoiled/drink has fouled
P	• Inflict a debility (from fear/cold/ennui/ hunger/fatigue/nausea/despair/etc.)
P	• Eat away at their gear, have it fail for no good reason
P	• Trap them in a maze of time/space/ perception
P	• Threaten/hinder/grab/tear at them with the environment
P	• Corrupt them (page 430)

H3	Corruption
P	Threat (<i>affliction</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to make monstrous
P	The power of the Things Below can infuse a person, beast, or spirit, corrupting them.
P	This could happen when they…
E	call on the Things Below for power, intentionally or not
E	spend time in a <b>corrupted site</b> (page 422), one that's poisonous or worse
E	attempt to cleanse someone or something of corruption, and things go wrong
E	are harmed/infected by an <b>artifact</b> (page 424) or <b>emanation</b> (page 436) of the Things Below, by one of <b>those</b> <b>who bear their taint</b> (next page), or by a <b>corrupted being</b> (page 432).
P	Add these to the list of GM moves for afflictions:
P	• Give them a gift (page 432), or increase one's potency
P	• Inflict a mark upon them (page 432), or make one worse
H2	PCs and corruption
P	If a PC possesses a <b>major arcana</b> associated with the <b>Things Below</b> (page 427), then the arcana's mysteries and consequences reflect the PC's growing corruption. Likewise, the <b>Thrall</b> playbook insert (<i>Book I</i>, page 152) reflects a PC being corrupted by the Things Below. If a PC has one of those arcana or inserts, allow its mechanics to drive their corruption. Don't give them additional gifts or marks unless they are corrupted in some additional way.
P	Should a PC become corrupted by the Things Below without gaining a major arcana or insert, then ask the player how they want to handle it.
P	Do they see the corruption as a threat to their character, something to rid themselves of and struggle against? If so, write it up as a threat (threat type:
P	<i>affliction</i>) and focus on increasingly problematic marks. But if the player wants to explore the power that's now available to them, and the cost of that power, then create a playbook insert for them, using the Thrall insert as inspiration.

H3	Corrupted being
P	To create a corrupted being, start with the original NPC, threat, or monster stats and consider how or why it was <b>corrupted</b> (page 430). If the being is a spirit and it normally would have a <b>sacred site</b> (page 362), create it as a <b>corrupted site</b> (page 422) instead.
P	Identify the themes (page 416), aspects, and instinct (page 417) of the Thing Below responsible for the corruption. Then pick or roll gifts and marks, up to 3 of each.
P	<b>1d12</b> gift
HR
P	1 A terrifying presence/aura/gaze
P	2 An ability to pass unnoticed (in certain conditions)
P	3 Immunity to certain harms (poison, disease, fire, cold, drowning, etc.)
P	4 Mind games/false sensations, inflicted on others
P	5 Minion(s)/spirit(s)/creature(s), always lurking or called up as needed
P	6 Regeneration/rejuvenation/ immortality
P	7 Serendipity/luck/hexes/misfortune, bestowed on others
P	8 Some power to torment/bind/harm at range
P	9 Transformation/mutation/growth
P	10 Uncanny insight/inexplicable knowledge
P	11 Unnatural resilience (Armor 4 except vs. bronze, +4 HP)
P	12 Vicious/terrible/mighty physical attacks
P	<b>1d12</b> mark
HR
P	1 Contagion/pollution/transmission of their corruption
P	2 Compulsions (per <b>whispers and</b> <b>visions</b>, page 428)
P	3 Intolerance (to something natural/ pure/sacred)
P	4 Nightmares/visions/hallucinations
P	5 Physical mutations (scales, reptilian eyes, claws, warped limbs, etc.)
P	6 Some sort of taboo (can't cross a line of salt, can't lie, etc.)
P	7 Strange appetites/needs/fascinations
P	8 Unhealthy/unnatural appearance
P	9 Unwholesome presence (puts children/natural beasts on edge)
P	10 Unnatural signs (no shadow, no reflection, aura of cold, etc.)
P	11 Vulnerability to bronze (its touch burns, its presence distracts)
P	12 Wounds that heal slowly (but they regain HP normally)
P	Consider these gifts and marks in light of the Thing and original being. How has their corruption made them both more and less than what they once were? Revise their stats, tags, qualities, and moves to reflect all of the above. Add the <i>corrupted</i> tag.
P	If the being is a spirit, alter its manifestation to reflect the themes and aspects of the Thing that corrupts it. Bronze weapons can always harm a manifest corrupted spirit, and might ignore its armor.
P	How has corruption changed the being's behavior? Are they merely a conduit for their master's instinct? Do they struggle to maintain their own identity? Has their corruption combined with their original personality in an unusual way? Rewrite their instinct to suit.

ICON	icons/aberration.svg
H3	Emanation
P	The Things Below are well and truly trapped—bound within the earth, <i>to</i> the earth. Even during the Time of Cataclysm, they did not walk free. They are tethered as long as the world remains.
P	But there are cracks in the world. Places where their influence bubbles up. Deep water is the surest of these, which is why it is often filled with horrors. But any place can bear their taint.
P	The power of the Things Below usually just corrupts what's already there. But sometimes, it coalesces. It creates something new, something terrible. A spirit or being with a will and purpose of its own.
P	Scholars call these "emanations." They are not truly part of a Thing Below. They are...
P	discharge. Leavings. Spawn.
P	To create an emanation, identify the Thing Below it spawned from, including its themes (page 416), aspects, and instinct (page 417). Identify, too, the <b>corrupted site</b> (page 422) it inhabits. Pick or roll for its origin.
P	1d12 origin
HR
P	1-2 Arose in the aftermath of great devastation/atrocity
P	3-4 Burst forth from a <b>corrupted being</b> (page 432) that absorbed too much power
P	5-6 Called forth, via a terrible ritual
P	7-8 Given shape by worship/adoration/ feeding
P	9-10 Let into the world by accident/ hubris, a failed attempt to bind/ cleanse/wield the power of the Things Below
P	11-12 Spawned spontaneously from a truly <b>corrupted site</b> (page 422) Imagine the emanation that forms as a result. It will share at least some of the themes and aspects of the Thing from which it spawned, and might share its instinct. An emanation has its own memory, arguably its own personality. It might communicate with its progenitor, or do its bidding, but an emanation is its own thing.

H3	Hand of Daagon
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>emanation</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>curious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 23; <b>Armor</b> 4 (resilience), 0 vs. bronze <b>Damage</b> many hands d12+1 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>grabby</i>, ignores armor)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> blind; tremorsense; reaches through matter like it was water
P	<b>Instinct</b> to feed the Mouth
P	• Sink into the stone, or emerge from it
P	• Provoke abject revulsion
P	• Reach through armor, clothing, flesh, bone to take what is most valued
P	• Retreat with its prize, back to the water
P	In a deep deep cave, where light has never shined, there is a lake. In that lake, there is a Mouth of Daagon: ever-hungry, evergreedy, consuming all that it is offered.
P	And in the caverns around that lake? There you will find the Hand: ever-groping, ever-grasping, dragging all it finds of value back to the Mouth.
HR
ICON	icons/aberration.svg
H3	Voice of the Eternal Maw
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>spirit</i>, <i>emanation</i>, <i>devious</i>, <i>terrifying</i>, <i>hungry</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 19; <b>Armor</b> 4 (resilience), 0 vs. bronze <b>Damage</b> scream d10 (<i>near</i>, <i>area</i>, <i>reload</i>, ignores armor) or unnaturally large and toothy maw d10+2 (<i>hand</i>, <i>messy</i>,
P	3 piercing)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> tethered to the vortex, unable to leave the mountain <b>Instinct</b> to create more mouths, more wraiths
P	• Compel someone with <b>whispers</b> (see page 428), even from afar
P	• Possess a traveler, especially one who is hungry, weary, or tired
P	• Drive its host to feast
P	• Leave its host corrupted, withering, doomed to become a <b>wraith</b> (page 79)
P	Hidden in the southern arm of the Huffel Peaks, there is a gorge that splits a mountain. The gorge is cloaked in constantly churning mist, cold and clammy. At the base of the gorge is a thin split in reality, a vortex, a manifestation of Hlad the Devourer, sucking in everything it touches.
P	The mountain and the gorge are shunned now. The <b>Hillfolk</b> (page 228) and the <b>Ustrina</b> (page 464) who live nearby know better than to approach. But the <b>Barrow</b> <b>Builders</b> (page 34) fed the vortex. They brought it gifts, and offerings, and living, screaming sacrifice. In time, these offerings gave the vortex a Voice. And the Voice roams the mountain still.
